headline: High: TREK’s browser/MCP, shared files, and sensitive secrets create default-path risks when paired with langchain4j’s file/network-capable LLM workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK can use browsers and MCP, and its AI is built into a real-time collaborative planner; langchain4j is an LLM framework that can ingest external content. A shared filesystem or MCP bridge is not explicitly documented between them, so the injection path is inferred rather than proven. The pathway is plausible in default integrations, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF TREK exposes browser/MCP content to langchain4j prompts without provenance filtering, injection is possible.
IF the two agents are connected through a shared workspace or message bridge, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt ingestion from browser/MCP outputs.
Add provenance tags and strip instructions from untrusted content.
Require human review before langchain4j acts on TREK-generated text.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization middleware between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches reservations, documents, photos, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while langchain4j is a general LLM framework with network egress none in its profile but no explicit local-only guarantee for all deployments. If TREK data is passed into langchain4j prompts or logs, sensitive data can leak through model inputs or downstream outputs. The pairwise path is plausible and the blast radius is large.
conditions: IF TREK sends any of its sensitive data classes into langchain4j prompts, leakage risk exists.
IF TREK logs or exports prompt context containing secrets, those secrets can be retained in files or outputs.
mitigations: Redact secrets before any cross-agent handoff.
Block API keys and MFA secrets from prompt context.
Keep TREK logs separate from langchain4j inputs.
Review file-sharing paths for documents and photos.
requires-engineering: implement field-level data-loss prevention.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: TREK has allowlisted network egress, browser use, MCP, and shared collaborative sessions with multiple instances; langchain4j can participate in LLM workflows but its write surfaces are not specified. Because overlapping write or coordination primitives are not documented for langchain4j, the conflict is inferred and uncertainty pushes severity upward from low. The pair can still contend over shared mutable resources if orchestrated together.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared resource through MCP, API, or filesystem, conflicts can occur.
IF TREK runs multiple collaborative sessions against the same backing store, stale writes become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate writable directories per agent.
Serialize writes to shared resources.
Disable concurrent edits during cross-agent workflows.
Use optimistic-lock checks on shared records.
requires-engineering: add transaction or lock coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in, so it may act on generated travel decisions; langchain4j can supply those decisions or text. If TREK treats langchain4j output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into bookings, reservations, or user-facing plans. The downstream blast radius includes irreversible or costly actions, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF TREK consumes langchain4j output without a verification step, cascading errors can propagate.
IF TREK uses generated text to update reservations or user-facing plans, mistakes become costly.
mitigations: Require confirmation before any booking or reservation action.
Show source citations next to generated recommendations.
Add a verification step for dates, prices, and locations.
Limit autonomous actions to draft mode.
requires-engineering: add policy checks before write actions.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles reservations, documents, photos, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while langchain4j is a general LLM framework with no residency or retention controls shown here. If TREK data flows into langchain4j-hosted or logged processing, compliance gaps around sensitive travel and account data are plausible. The other agent is not cited for residency because its profile lacks such controls.
conditions: IF TREK processes EU personal data through langchain4j without a DPA or residency control, compliance risk exists.
IF secrets handled by TREK are logged or retained by cross-agent processing, policy violations can occur.
mitigations: Confirm data-processing terms for any external LLM endpoint.
Exclude secrets from prompts and logs.
Document retention periods for shared artifacts.
Restrict cross-border transfer of travel records.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and retention controls.
